title: Composable scope lattice and actionability model for RBAC v2
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design a composable RBAC v2 role model that expresses resource hierarchy, multi-scope membership (a lattice), and an actionability model that maps roles to fine-grained permissions. This ticket captures the decision record, example matrices, migration considerations from RBAC v1, audit integration points, and SSO/SAML attribute mapping requirements.
background: Current RBAC implementation is flat and tenant-scoped; it lacks composability for cross-tenant admin scopes (e.g., org-level, project-level, model-level) and forces brittle role proliferation. We need a model that reduces role explosion, supports least privilege, and gives audit logs clear provenance for policy evaluation.
goals: 1) Define canonical resource hierarchy and scope lattice semantics. 2) Specify role composition rules and permission resolution algorithm. 3) Produce an initial permission matrix for common admin and operator personas. 4) Ensure audit logging captures decision provenance. 5) Define SAML/SSO attribute mappings for federated roles.
non_goals: Not implementing the runtime enforcement or migration tooling in this ticket; those are separate engineering tickets. Not reworking RBAC UIs in Console beyond required display fields.
proposed_model_summary: Roles are sets of action-capability tuples bound to one or more scopes. Scopes form a lattice (global > org > project > resource) allowing inheritance and explicit deny precedence. Role composition supports 'role templates' and 'composite roles' (union of roles with conflict resolution). Permission resolution uses ordered rules: explicit deny, explicit allow at nearest scope, inherited allow, default deny.
resource_hierarchy_examples:
Examples:
- global (all customers)
- org:org_42
- project:org_42:proj_7
- model:org_42:proj_7:model_gpt4x
Each resource node is addressable by canonical path. Scopes may also include environment tags (e.g., staging/production) and dedicated pools (e.g., dedicated:gpu-pool-3).
actionability_concepts: Atomic actions (read, list, create, update, delete, manage_keys, manage_rollouts, impersonate) used to form higher-level capabilities. An actionability matrix maps each role to allowed actions per resource type and scope. We will support action parameters (e.g., generate: max_tokens) for future rate-limited actions.
permission_matrix_summary: Initial persona rows: Billing Admin, Org Admin, Project Owner, Model Deployer, Support Engineer, Read-only Auditor. Columns are resource types and canonical actions. Example: Billing Admin -> (org:billing:update) at org scope; Support Engineer -> (read, impersonate-session) at project scope; Read-only Auditor -> (read, list, export) at org/project scope with write denied.
conflict_resolution: Rules: 1) Explicit deny anywhere wins. 2) Explicit allow at the same scope wins over inherited allow from a parent scope. 3) Composite roles follow deny-first semantics when combining. 4) In ambiguous cases, evaluation returns decision='need_review' and logs full provenance for operator review.
audit_logging_integration: Audit entries must include: actor, effective_role_set, evaluated_scopes, matching_policies, decision (allow|deny|need_review), evaluation_timestamp, request_trace_id, and optional SAML assertion id. Logs should be structured JSON for ingestion into Elastic/BigQuery and include a compact human-readable summary for Console display.
sso_saml_mapping: We will support mapping SAML attributes to scope-bound role assertions. Mapping modes: attribute->role (static), attribute->scope (dynamic), and assertion of composite roles. Recommended SAML attributes: Role, Organization, ProjectList. Default mapping rules, plus a tenant-level override UI for admins. Documentation will include examples for Okta and Azure AD.
migration_strategy: Phase 0: parallel evaluation mode - new RBAC engine evaluates but enforcement stays on v1; generate discrepancy reports. Phase 1: opt-in enforcement for non-critical routes; provide guided role migration tool. Phase 2: full enforcement and deprecation of v1. Rollback plan: global feature flag and emergency allowlist. Migration must include a scripts set to map common v1 roles to templates and flag uncertain mappings.
console_and_api_changes: API additions: /rbac/v2/evaluate, /rbac/v2/roles (role templates), /rbac/v2/assignments. Console: role explorer showing effective permissions per scope and an audit view that surfaces decision provenance. All APIs must be backward compatible; add v2 namespace.
security_and_compliance_notes: Design must satisfy auditability for SOC2/ISO requirements: immutable logs, exportable retention policy, and proof of evaluation for each privileged action. KMS/HSM integration for signing migration bundles is recommended.
acceptance_criteria: Decision record checked in and reviewed by Security and Product
Permission matrix draft covering 8 common personas with example mappings
Audit schema defined and sample log produced by a simulation script
SAML mapping spec with Okta and Azure AD examples
Migration phases and rollback plan documented
deliverables: Permission matrix CSV attached to PRD
SAML mapping examples (Okta, Azure AD) in docs
Stakeholder review notes and approval thread
notes: Prefer conservative initial defaults: deny-by-default, explicit allow, and comprehensive logging. Keep role templates small and composable to avoid explosion. We will iterate on UI metaphors after testing with early enterprise customers.
open_questions: How to represent temporary elevated roles (just-in-time access) in the lattice?
Do we need an audit-only mode on a per-route basis or just global?
Should 'impersonate' be modeled as an action or a wrapper capability with stricter logging?
What SLAs do we require for policy-evaluation latency to meet 99th percentile API latency SLOs?
